question_text: A 45-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with fever, cough, tonsillar enlargement, and bleeding lips. She has a diffuse blistering rash that encompasses the palms and soles of her feet, in total covering 55% of her total body surface area (TBSA). The upper epidermal layer easily slips away with slight rubbing. Within 24 hours the rash progresses to 88% TBSA involvement and the patient requires mechanical ventilation for respiratory distress.
